COL.head: We gave Colorado a 70% chance, and they delivered.

LAK.head: We gave Los Angeles only a 30% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Darcy Kuemper got lit up
surprises.body: Kuemper allowed 8 goals on 29 shots, worth 3.3 expected goals: 4.7 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 600 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

surprises.head: Colorado’s power play did damage
surprises.body: 4 power-play goals on 5 chances. A power play like theirs against a kill like Los Angeles’s scores 4 or more about once every 40 games.

story.head: The Avalanche pile it on the Kings
paras: Brock Nelson got the scoring started for the Avalanche on the power play early in the first. Brian Dumoulin tied it up for Los Angeles late in the period, and Parker Kelly put the Avalanche back ahead 2-1 less than three minutes later. There were six goals in the second period alone. Nathan MacKinnon made it 3-1 on the power play just 23 seconds into the period, but Joel Armia cut Colorado’s lead to 3-2 shorthanded just over a minute later. MacKinnon scored his second of the night midway through the period to make it 4-2 for the Avalanche. Nicolas Roy made it 5-2 late in the period, but Trevor Moore made it 5-3 shorthanded less than two minutes later. Artturi Lehkonen stretched the lead to 6-3 on the power play 44 seconds later. Midway through the third, With the goalie pulled, Artemi Panarin cut it to 6-4, and Brandt Clarke and MacKinnon squared off. Gabriel Landeskog and Lehkonen scored just over a minute apart with just under six minutes left to make it 8-4, and the Kings had no answer. Erik Haula made his Kings debut, after two seasons with the Predators, and picked up an assist. Jaden Schwartz made his Avalanche debut, after five seasons with the Kraken, and picked up two assists. Nelson finished with a goal and two assists.
Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Mackenzie Blackwood made 27 saves for the Avalanche, and Darcy Kuemper allowed eight goals on 29 shots.

Special teams did the work: the Avalanche scored four power-play goals on five chances and killed all four Kings power plays. The Avs moved to 1-0-0, tied for first in the NHL in points, while the Kings dropped to 0-1-0, still last in the NHL.

items.text: The Kings scored twice shorthanded in the second, their first time doing that since Dec 7, 2024.
It was the first game of the season for both teams, and the Avalanche won their home opener.
Nathan MacKinnon has a point in all nine of his games against Los Angeles since 2023-24.
